column1: # HsapDv Developmental Stage Mapping Table
# Maps donor ages to Human Developmental Stages ontology (HsapDv) terms.
# CxG schema 6.0.0 requires descendants of HsapDv:0000001 for Homo sapiens.
# All 287 donors in this atlas are adult females (age range 19-69 where recorded).
# HsapDv:0000087 ("human adult stage") covers all adults >= 19 years.
# This is the broadest valid term and is universally accepted by CxG for adult samples.
# More specific year-based terms exist (e.g., HsapDv:0000246 = "25 year-old human stage")
# but HsapDv:0000087 is standard practice for atlases and avoids the problem of
# 126 Kumar donors who only have binary age (young/old, no continuous value).
# Source: external_studies/outputs/harmonized_metadata/harmonized_donor_metadata.csv
# Generated: 2026-02-11
# Plan: A2_ontology_mappings

# Age data completeness by study:

#   murrow:  28/28 donors have age_continuous (range 19-39)

# Kumar age issue:
#   Kumar et al. 2023 (Nature) reported 126 donors with binary age classification only.
#   The paper's methods define young = premenopausal, old = postmenopausal.
#   No continuous ages were published. These donors still map to HsapDv:0000087
#   since all are confirmed adults. The binary distinction is captured in age_binary
#   and menopausal_status_binary metadata columns, not in the ontology mapping.
# If year-specific HsapDv terms are ever needed for the 161 donors with continuous age:
#   HsapDv:0000246 = 25 year-old human stage (19-25 range)
#   ... etc. up to HsapDv:0000290+ for 69-year range
#   But this level of granularity is not required or expected by CxG.
